problem: Robot navigation depends on accurate metric maps and localisation built from first-hand sensing, so abundant pre-existing but abstract and metrically inaccurate 2D maps (sketches, floor-plans, satellite maps) go unused. Prior sketch- and floor-plan-based systems are tailored to one map type and assume metric accuracy.
motivation: Humans navigate with abstract maps by reading them as sequences of navigational behaviours such as 'follow corridor' or 'turn right', and localise using visual affordance cues rather than metric position. The paper hypothesises that a behaviour-based topological representation lets robots navigate with limited metric information and use readily available maps without prior traversal.
key_idea: Represent the environment as a Scene Action Map (SAM), a topological graph of changepoint/destination nodes joined by navigational-behaviour edges, learn to read SAMs from varied 2D maps, and navigate on them with affordance-based localisation and learned behaviours.
insight: Only the behavioural and topological structure of a map is needed for navigation, so noisy predicted SAMs cost little: the PC drop versus human-annotated SAMs is small. Adding explicit changepoint-proximity detection to the localiser is crucial, since the Graphnav heuristic switches behaviours too late at 0.8 m/s (Easy hand-drawn SR 45.5 vs 70.0). Augmenting GLN training by randomly changing an edge's behaviour improves robustness to noisy predicted SAMs, notably Hard floor-plan SR 0 to 50.
method: SAM representation: directed graph whose nodes are changepoints or user-given destinations and whose edges each carry one behaviour from a set of N (turn-left / go-forward / turn-right); each node has at most one outgoing edge per behaviour so localisation is well defined.

Node prediction (CPNet): MobileNetv2 CNN scores map patches as changepoints. It is trained with SupCon then BCE fine-tuning. Grid-sampled points are thresholded and clustered with GrowCompactClusters, keeping the top-scoring point per cluster.

Edge prediction (EMNet + Sinkhorn): a CNN takes a crop of the map plus rasterised K nearest-neighbour node channels and outputs a K×N score matrix. A Sinkhorn layer with a dustbin row/column gives a partial soft assignment of behaviours to neighbours. Trained with SupCon then an assignment loss, using multi-scale networks merged by preferring shorter edges.

SAM Localisation System: a Graphnav-style Graph Localisation Network encodes a depth-image sequence and matches it via a GNN to the SAM crop, scoring edges as the robot's edge pose. A new 3-layer MLP head predicts changepoint proximity, and the loss is xent(edge scores) + λ·xent(changepoint scores).

Changepoint detector: temporally smooths and thresholds the changepoint score to trigger the next behaviour switch early, avoiding overshoot at higher speed; destination nodes halt after a preset distance along the edge.
Planner and behaviours: Dijkstra over the SAM from the current edge pose, replanning if the edge pose deviates. Execution uses DECISION obstacle-avoiding path-following behaviours.
Robustness augmentation: during GLN training, randomly change the behaviour label of one edge in the SAM crop (the augmented variant is called GLN+EA in the paper's results).

setting.backbone: MobileNetv2 (CPNet, EMNet, trained from scratch/SupCon+finetune); Graphnav-style GLN with GNN; DECISION learned behaviour controller
setting.training_data: Small custom datasets of hand-drawn maps and floor-plans of campus buildings with manually annotated SAMs, and satellite maps of industrial areas annotated from OpenStreetMap; a separate map-reading model per map type; GLN trained per Graphnav's method with edge-behaviour augmentation
setting.observation: 3 RealSense D435i RGB-D cameras (140° FoV combined), depth image sequence used for localisation; 2D maps as input for map-reading
setting.action_space: discrete navigational behaviours (turn-left, go-forward, turn-right) executed by the DECISION controller, at ~0.8 m/s
setting.privileged: none (uses pre-existing 2D maps; destination nodes user-specified)

numbers_note: No standard benchmark; results are on a custom real-world Spot robot indoor test (Easy/Med/Hard routes) and map-reading precision/recall, so no canonical-benchmark entries. Key custom results: Table 1 map-reading (Pr/Re) hand-drawn node 0.848/0.975, edge+behaviour 0.667/0.535; floor-plan node 0.732/0.779, edge+behaviour 0.630/0.494; satellite node 0.865/0.621, edge+behaviour 0.761/0.662. Table 2 navigation SR_Nav/PC_Nav on predicted SAMs with GLN+EA: hand-drawn Easy 80.0/90.0, Med 62.5/75.0, Hard 50.0/85.0; floor-plan Easy 62.5/71.9, Med 37.5/65.6, Hard 50.0/80.0.
results: On human-annotated hand-drawn Easy routes, the changepoint-aware localiser reaches 70.0 SR vs 45.5 for Graphnav's; on floor-plans it reaches 66.7 vs 12.5. On predicted SAMs, GLN+EA generally performs best, reaching Hard-route SR 50.0 on both hand-drawn and floor-plan maps at 50-100 m with a Spot robot. Map-reading gets node precision/recall of 0.73-0.87/0.62-0.98 but edge-with-behaviour recall of only 0.49-0.66.
limitations: Constrained to a specific behaviour set (path-following turn/forward), which handles open spaces poorly and ties the map to robot dynamics.
Behaviour assignment on edges is error-prone (go-forward vs turn confusion), and edge recall is low; occlusion and open areas cause node errors.
Small real-world test scale (few trials per setting, one indoor environment), with Med/Hard success rates still low; destination halting is heuristic.
compares_to: Graphnav localisation with heuristic behaviour switching
